subject: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for Fintech Labs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / prompt collection

Thanks again for the time today, Sofia — really helpful to walk through the primary workflows and the three high-risk areas you flagged (transaction disambiguation, regulatory redaction, and edge-case fraud scenarios). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Recommended model candidates (based on latency/cost/quality tradeoffs we discussed):
  - Redwood-3-small (good latency, strong on instruction following)
  - Open-LLM/neox-20b (better for longer-context transactional reasoning)
  - Redwood-qa-finetune (if you want higher accuracy on domain Q&A)

- Benchmarks / artifacts I shared: Redwood internal benchmark summary (link below) and a short model-fit questionnaire I attached.

Action items / ask from Fintech Labs:
1) Can you share a sample prompt set & representative edge cases (CSV or JSONL works) — include examples that contain PII and ones that require redaction/normalization. Mark anything that is sensitive.
2) If possible, include a short golden-label set (20–50 examples) for the fraud & regulatory cases so we can run early quality checks.
3) Any redaction policies or internal compliance notes you want the eval team to follow (e.g., token-level retention, hashing vs placeholder).

Next steps from us:
- Nikhil (cc’d) will propose an eval plan + instrumentation (canary + continuous regression detection) once we see the prompts.
- I’ll follow up with a tailored cost/throughput estimate for the two top model candidates.

Attachments: model-fit-questionnaire.pdf (short form to help structure the prompt dump).
Shared links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwoodFintechBenchmarks

Proposed follow-up meeting: Friday next week to review the prompt set and pick the canary slice — does 10am PT on 5 Mar work for your team?

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@fintechlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-team@fintechlabs.com
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / prompt collection

Thanks Marissa — great recap and yes the 5 Mar slot looks good from my side. Quick responses to your asks and a short sample attached: prompts_sample.csv.

- We can provide a larger dump (CSV) but need guidance on redaction. Our current policy: mask full PANs/account numbers, but we prefer retaining last-4 for user flows. For some regulatory responses we have to keep exact timestamps and transaction IDs.
- Concern: we need to understand how Redwood will detect regressions in production prompts (we want proactive alerts for hallucinations / incorrect regulatory responses).
- Attached: 10 sample prompts (some intentionally include PII placeholders) — this should give an idea of the distribution.

Also copying our engineering address (eng-team@fintechlabs.com) — they’ll attach a larger set and a short README.

On redaction: we’d likely prefer placeholders (e.g., <ACCOUNT_ID>) over hashing because several downstream systems need deterministic mapping, but we’re open to options if you have recommendations.

Sofia
Director of Product, Fintech Labs
sofia.alvarez@fintechlabs.com
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@finwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / prompt collection

Hi Sofia — thanks for the sample and the redaction note. Quick answers and a suggested plan from the engineering side: 

1) Regression detection / metrics:
   - We recommend a canary + continuous eval approach: run a canary slice of production prompts through the candidate model and monitor per-prompt metrics (confidence, token-level perplexity) plus periodic human checks for hallucination rate.
   - For your workflow we’ll track: intent accuracy (for transaction classification), entity extraction F1 (for KYC fields), and a domain-hallucination metric (percentage of responses failing a ruleset).
   - We’ll hook these into Redwood Console alerts (we can create a per-route dashboard) and set thresholds for automatic rollback to a safe model if hallucination rate crosses X% over a 24h window.

2) Redaction guidance:
   - Placeholder approach (e.g., <ACCOUNT_ID>, <PAN_LAST4>) is fine and recommended if downstream systems need deterministic mapping. Avoid hashing if you rely on consistent, reversible mapping across systems.
   - For privacy-sensitive audit logs, we can store redaction mappings in a customer-managed KMS-backed store if you need reversible mapping for support cases — we can include this as an option in the Private deployment.

3) Prompt formatting & sizing:
   - Best: CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, label (optional), pii_flag (yes/no), pii_fields (comma-separated). For evaluation, a 5–10k prompt dump is enough to get meaningful throughput / cost estimates; 200–500 labeled examples across the key failure modes gives a strong canary set.

4) Quick artifacts attached: benchmark-summary-Redwood-3.pdf (short model comparison) and a sample eval run. Drive link with more detailed results: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwoodFintechBenchmarks

If you want, we can also supply a small prompt sanitizer script to convert your CSV to our canonical JSONL (sanitizing placeholders) — happy to run that for the first dump.

-Nikhil
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / prompt collection

Sofia — thanks for the sample and for looping in engineering. Two quick operational asks so we can move this to an eval kickoff next week:

1) Can your eng team upload the full prompt dump to the Drive folder above or send a CSV attachment. Please include a column named pii_flag with values yes/no and a brief notes column for any special redaction rules per row. We’ll treat uploads according to the placeholder guidance (we’ll keep placeholders as-is).

2) If you can provide 200–300 labeled examples for the three priority failure modes (transaction disambiguation, regulatory responses, fraud edge-cases) by EOD Wed (4 Mar), Nikhil can get a canary eval running and share initial results by Friday.

3) For contractual/compliance: if you prefer, we can put a short data handling addendum in the SOW. I can route a DocuSign for signature — let me know and I’ll send it today.

Attachments we expect with the dump: prompts_full.csv (or prompts_full.jsonl), a README.txt describing fields, and the pii-aware sample mapping if you use placeholders.

If time permits on the 5 Mar call we’ll walk through the initial canary dashboard and decide which model variant to pressure-test further.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for 5 Mar 10am PT once you confirm.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
